media:group.media:title: QSolid Outlook for 2026
media:group.media:description:
The final year of QSolid has officially begun. In this video, our Coordinator Frank Wilhelm-Mauch shares his vision for a successful completion of the project and the key challenges that still lie ahead.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de LinkedIn: / qsolid X: / qsolid_de Bluesky: @qsolid.bsky.social

media:group.media:title: QSolid Review of 2025
media:group.media:description:
2025 marks an important year for QSolid. Watch the video to discover how our consortium team successfully integrated the prototype quantum computer into the Jülich Supercomputing Centre’s infrastructure and further advanced its hardware and software.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de LinkedIn: / qsolid X: / qsolid_de Bluesky: @qsolid.bsky.social

media:group.media:title: QSolid Outlook for 2025
media:group.media:description:
Now that the consortium has reached the mid-term milestone on the way to Germany's first quantum computer with improved error correction, QSolid coordinator Prof. Frank Wilhelm-Mauch (Forschungszentrum Jülich) talks about the team's plans for the second half of the project.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE

media:group.media:title: QSolid Review of 2024
media:group.media:description:
The year 2024 marks a major milestone for the QSolid team: the completion of the prototype for Germany's first quantum computer with a low error rate. Project leader Prof. Frank Wilhelm-Mauch (Forschungszentrum Jülich) explains the work done and operational plans for the prototype.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE

media:group.media:title: QSolid Outlook for 2024
media:group.media:description:
In an interview, QSolid project coordinator Prof. Dr Frank Wilhelm-Mauch from Forschungszentrum Jülich outlines the goals and challenges the consortium faces in 2024.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Review of 2023
media:group.media:description:
In an interview, QSolid project coordinator Prof. Dr Frank Wilhelm-Mauch from Forschungszentrum Jülich looks back at project achievements and challenges overcome in 2023.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Tommaso Calarco
media:group.media:description:
In QSolid, Prof. Tommaso Calarco leads the team of the Institute for Quantum Control at Forschungszentrum Jülich. He gives us the big picture around QSolid: What is the significance of our project for science, industry and society in general and for Germany as a business location in particular? What are the challenges on the way to the first German quantum computer?
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Benjamin Lilienthal-Uhlig
media:group.media:description:
Dr Benjamin Lilienthal-Uhlig from Fraunhofer IPMS leads the Fraunhofer team in QSolid. He gives us insights into the work of the two Fraunhofer institutes involved, and other partners, on an integrated solution for the QPU and the CMOS control chips to control the qubits on our targeted quantum computer.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Stefan Rombouts
media:group.media:description:
Dr Stefan Rombouts from ParityQC heads the HPC Integration working group in QSolid. He reports on how work is already underway to integrate the envisaged quantum computer into a high performance computing environment.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Shai Machnes
media:group.media:description:
As CEO of Qruise, Dr Shai Machnes leads his team in QSolid. He is one of the main people responsible for middle and firmware stack control in our project and explains to us where the challenges lie in working with qubits and how they are to be brought under control.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with David DiVincenzo
media:group.media:description:
Prof. Dr David DiVincenzo from Forschungszentrum Jülich is a theoretical physicist and heads the hardware modelling and theory working group in QSolid. He tells us how he and his team are using theoretical concepts and models to accompany the work of the experimental physicists and engineers in our project to realise the first German quantum computer.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Carsten Degenhardt
media:group.media:description:
Dr Carsten Degenhardt from Forschungszentrum Jülich, ZEA-2 leads the hardware integration technology working group in QSolid. He explains how room temperature electronics for the qubits work and why the further development towards cryogenic electronics is necessary.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid

media:group.media:title: QSolid Interview with Gregor Oelsner
media:group.media:description:
Dr Gregor Oelsner from Leibniz IPHT heads the Scaling Technology working group in QSolid. He explains what qubits actually are and goes into more detail about the QPU and scaling technology of our envisaged quantum computer.
Learn more about the project: www.q-solid.de X: https://twitter.com/QSolid_DE LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/showcase/qsolid
